fixture_name: Express-collector corridor planning study — Canada TAC planning (Toronto context, PD-licensed portal)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Decision-load mechanism from simultaneous transfer-permission and signage changes across three interchanges on an AADT 420,000 corridor is a genuine, plausible safety concern well-suited to a Planning Stage RSA.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Pivotal claim (avoiding collisions introduced elsewhere along the route) is backed by the verbatim EV-CA-003 quote, and scenario facts (AADT, change scope) rest on recorded corridor inputs; the inferential step is transparently labelled.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly filed as a safety_concern with null normative basis, keeping the human-factors safety issue categorically distinct from any compliance question under CRSAG semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and actionable: quarterly one-interchange staging with defined before/after speed-differential monitoring is measurable and viable at planning stage.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are not applicable on a controlled-access express-collector mainline, and the finding explicitly acknowledges this and scopes road users to vehicle occupants.

justifications.substance: Unresolved conflict between ministry and municipal continuity records genuinely threatens Planning Stage RSA scope completeness, risking exclusion of redistributed movements at interchanges outside the limits.
justifications.evidence_grounding: Verbatim quote EV-CA-007 captures both poles of the conflict (continuity 'must be maintained across all three' yet 'cannot be guaranteed' at Interchange 2), directly supporting the pivotal scope-ambiguity claim.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Correctly framed as a compliance/process question about scope record specification, kept categorically distinct from any asserted collision mechanism or geometric safety defect.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Specific and viable: names both records, assigns the ministry planning office as counterpart, and requires recording whether resolved continuity effects fall inside the audit boundary.
justifications.vru_coverage: Not applicable on the controlled-access mainline but explicitly acknowledged, including propagation of continuity outcomes to downstream arterials where VRUs travel, without overclaiming exposure.
